newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANZ Australia job ads rise 0.5 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANZ Australia job ads rise 0.5 pct in June.

text.p: The Australia and New Zealand (ANZ) Banking Group Ltd said on Monday its job advertisement series rose by 0.5 percent in June after a 7.3 percent fall in May, to see the series 2.4 percent higher over the past year.
In trend terms, the series rose by 1.4 percent in June, comapred with 1.8 percent in May and 2.2 percent in April.
ANZ said the trend series had been positive for seven consecutive months after declining for 22 months between February 1995 and November 1996.
"Demand for labour is increasing, but at a fairly slow pace," ANZ chief economist Saul Eslake said in a statement.
The analysis of recent trends was complicated by large fluctuations in the series in April and May due to Easter falling earlier than usual.

Eslake said a sensible way of looking through the fluctuations was to note the number of job ads in the June quarter was 6.4 percent higher than the March quarter, which in turn was 4.2 percent higher than in the December quarter.
"The level of job advertising over the past three months is broadly consistent with net new job creation averaging around 13,000 per month over the next three months," he said.

"This is a little below the figures suggested by the number of job advertisements earlier this year, but nonetheless compares favourably with actual net job losses averaging 3,200 per month between December and May," Eslake said.

Assuming the 40,300 fall in May employment was reversed in the June data released this Thursday, Eslake said that jobs growth would need to average at least 20,000 per month during 1997/98 (July/June) to meet the government's forecast of two percent growth for the year.

"Alternatively, if employment growth averages, say, 15,000 per month in the first half of 1997/98, as seems plausible, the pace of net new job creation would need to step up to an average of 35,000 per month in the second half of the year in order to meet the Budget forecast," Eslake said.
The ANZ said trend growth in job advertisements negative in the ACT and Tasmania, but was rising -- at a diminishing pace -- in other states.

The ANZ also said that due to one Victorian newspapers inability to supply figures for the final week of June, the Victorian figure was estimated based on the first three weeks of the month. As a result the June Victorian, and national, figure were subject to revision next month.
